title: Flat constant extension and K-flat tensor of pro-zero cone towers
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $A$ a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $R=\underline A$ its constant ring sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and $R\to\mathcal O$ a flat map of commutative ring sheaves [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. For an $A$-complex $X$, put $E(X)=\mathcal O\otimes_R\underline X$, termwise. Let $v_n:X_n\to Y_n$ be a strict map of inverse sequences of $A$-complexes, whose cone tower is pro-zero in $D(A)$: for every $n$, some transition $\operatorname{Cone}(v_m)\to\operatorname{Cone}(v_n)$, $m\geq n$, is zero. Use derived categories and mapping cones [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], sheaf tensor and total tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For every possibly unbounded K-flat $\mathcal O$-complex $P$ [def-pc-kflat-complex], the strict map
$$P\otimes_{\mathcal O}E(X_\bullet)\longrightarrow P\otimes_{\mathcal O}E(Y_\bullet)$$
has a pro-zero cone tower in $D(\mathcal O)$ and induces an isomorphism on total right derived inverse limits of strict towers [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. If compatible chain maps $A[0]\to X_n,Y_n$ make $v_n$ commute with their units, that isomorphism carries the induced map $P\to R\lim(P\otimes E(X_n))$ to $P\to R\lim(P\otimes E(Y_n))$. These maps are the strict cones followed by the K-injective derived-limit comparison, not independently chosen maps in a triangulated category.

source.place: Tag 099M (lemma-naive-completion), transport of the Koszul pro-isomorphism; general flat constant-extension and tensor argument extracted by NE.

proof.text: The commutative constant module functor is exact by commutativeSiteConstantModuleFunctor_exact [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor]. Write U for restriction along R to O and L=U(O). Tensor cancellation [lem-pur-change-of-rings-tensor-cancellation-independent], with first argument the unit O, and the left unitor give a natural isomorphism E followed by U to tensorLeft L. The explicit site tensor functor in flatness agrees with monoidal tensorRight L by [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits]; symmetry identifies it with tensorLeft L. Hence E followed by U is exact by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. The forgetful functors to abelian sheaves preserve finite limits and colimits and reflect them [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. Their composites with E and U have the same underlying sheaf, so E is exact. Composing with exact constant realization gives exact flatConstantExtension.

source.place: Tags 093J, 03ER and 03DA, together with the tensor cancellation in Section 03EK.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to the exact extension functor. Its natural comparison identifies the derived image of a chain map with localization of the termwise image. For a transition f with Q_A(f)=0, compare naturality at f and at the zero map with the same endpoints; the termwise functor and Q send the latter to zero, so cancellation of the source comparison isomorphism gives Q_O(E(f))=0. Thus no null homotopy representative is chosen.

Put $T(B)=P\otimes_{\mathcal O}B$ with the direct-sum total differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. If $f:B\to B'$ is a quasi-isomorphism, $C(f)$ is acyclic by [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic]. The definition [def-pc-kflat-complex] makes $C(f)\otimes P$ acyclic. The signed interchange $p\otimes c\mapsto(-1)^{ij}c\otimes p$ in bidegree $(i,j)$ identifies $P\otimes C(f)$ with $C(f)\otimes P$: the two differential components agree using $(-1)^{(i+1)j}=(-1)^{ij+j}$ and $(-1)^{i(j+1)}=(-1)^{ij+i}$. This is a map on the direct sums with its inverse given by the same signs. The natural tensor-cone isomorphism [lem-pc-tensor-mapping-cone-iso] identifies $P\otimes C(f)$ with $C(T(f))$. Thus $C(T(f))$ is acyclic, and the same cone criterion makes $T(f)$ a quasi-isomorphism. This uses K-flatness alone, with no hypothesis on the individual terms of $P$.

The complex functor Q T inverts quasi-isomorphisms by Step 3, and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] supplies a lift T_D with natural isomorphism Q T_D = Q T. To transport an equation Q(f)=0, compare naturality of that isomorphism at f and at the zero chain map with the same endpoints. The left sides agree, while T and Q send the zero chain map to zero. Cancel the comparison isomorphism at the source to obtain Q(T(f))=0. This argument needs no separate inference of additivity for the lift.

source.place: Section 05RR, Definition 05RU: localization at quasi-isomorphisms; categories.tex Tag 04VG (lemma-properties-left-localization).

proof.text: An additive functor sends the mapping cone in complexes of towers to the cone of the transformed tower map; the resulting isomorphism is already an isomorphism of complexes of towers. For tensor transport, first compare the strict cone tower with the tower of levelwise cones using mappingCone.mapHomologicalComplexIso for each evaluation functor. The comparison commutes with tower transitions: compose with each of the two cone projections and use naturality of the original cone projections. The natural tensor-cone isomorphism [lem-pc-tensor-mapping-cone-iso], with its existing source-library hom_naturality lemma, then identifies the levelwise cone tower after left tensor by P with the cone tower of the tensor-transformed map. All comparisons are isomorphisms of strict towers.

source.place: Tag 014E (definition-cone), Tag 014F (lemma-functorial-cone) for strictly commuting squares; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YM (lemma-derived-tor-exact).

proof.text: Fix $n$ and choose $m\geq n$ such that the given transition $c_{mn}:C_m\to C_n$ has $Q_A(c_{mn})=0$. Steps 2 and 4 give $(T_DE_D)(Q_A(c_{mn}))=0$. By their natural comparisons, this says $Q_{\mathcal O}(TE(c_{mn}))=0$. The naturality in Step 5 identifies the transition $C(w_m)\to C(w_n)$ with $\theta_n\circ TE(c_{mn})\circ\theta_m^{-1}$, so its localization is zero as well. This proves the required pro-zero property with the very same $m$ as for the original cone tower. If $m=n$, the hypothesis says that $C_n$ is a zero object and the argument still applies.

source.place: Tag 099M (lemma-naive-completion), transport of the pro-isomorphism: explicit application of the localized functors and natural cone comparison.

proof.text:
Let $Z_\bullet=TE(X_\bullet)$ and $W_\bullet=TE(Y_\bullet)$, with strict map $w:Z_\bullet\to W_\bullet$. By Step 6 its strict cone tower is pro-zero in $D(\mathcal O)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] on the given small site with coefficient ring sheaf $\mathcal O$. It states precisely that the canonical map
$$u=R\lim(w):R\lim Z_\bullet\longrightarrow R\lim W_\bullet$$
is an isomorphism. This is the total right derived functor on the category of strict towers; the cited statement does not require exactness of countable products, boundedness of the complexes, or a uniform bound on the zero transitions.

source.place: Tag 0940 (section-derived-limits), Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok); pro-zero consequence as stated in the cited strict-tower theorem.

proof.text: Construct the coefficient-unit isomorphism explicitly. Constant realization of the regular module A maps to the regular module of the constant ring sheaf by the adjunction from constant module presheaves; the inverse sends a ring section r to r times the constant section 1. Sheafification hom extensionality and linearity show these maps are inverse. Ordinary scalar extension of the regular R-module to O is isomorphic to the regular O-module: sectionwise this is the tensor right unitor s tensor r mapped to s times phi(r); sheafify this presheaf isomorphism and compose with the sheafification counit. Transport these two isomorphisms through the fixed canonical extension model. The model map equation and naturality of toSheafify give precisely the normalization s tensor underline(a) mapped to s phi(underline(a)). Apply the single-complex comparison and the inverse tensor unitor to obtain the strict point P to T E(A[0]).

source.place: Tags 03CY and 093J for constant regular sections and sheafification; Section 03EK for tensor multiplication and the unit.

proof.text: For compatible strict coaugmentations alpha and beta with alpha followed by v equal to beta, whiskering by the strict complex functor preserves that equation. Naturality of the comparison eta at the strict tower-complex map identifies the two composites defining flatConstantPointedLimitMap. Functoriality of the ordinary limit and localization functors then gives the required unit equality. This works for every eta, so in particular for every total right-derived pair (RF, eta); no chain map between K-injective replacements needs to be chosen.

Unit compatibility is direct naturality of the specified comparison eta (sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0941).
